core_claim.P: The Distributor contract's dispute mechanism pauses Merkle tree updates while disputer != address(0); upon resolveDispute(false) the disputer resets to address(0), and setDisputeAmount reverts if disputer != address(0).
core_claim.I: The protocol should remain able to update the Merkle tree (updateTree) and the Governor should be able to adjust dispute parameters (disputeAmount, disputeToken) despite a malicious actor's dispute activity.
core_claim.V: A malicious actor can back-run resolveDispute(false) (same block or next block) to call disputeTree again, keeping disputer != address(0) nearly 100% of the time, so updateTree stays inaccessible and Governor setDisputeAmount calls consistently revert, at linear cost per cycle.

distinct_impacts.description: Reward distributions are halted because updateTree remains inaccessible.
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: Permanent Denial of Service: Reward distributions are halted. The updateTree function remains inaccessible.

distinct_impacts.description: Governance paralysis: administrators cannot adjust dispute parameters (disputeAmount, disputeToken) to make the attack economically unviable.
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: Governance Paralysis: Administrators cannot adjust dispute parameters (disputeAmount, disputeToken) to make the attack economically unviable.

distinct_impacts.description: Attacker back-runs resolveDispute(false) in the same block or submits in the next block to call disputeTree again, immediately re-locking the contract.
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: An attacker can back-run this transaction in the same block (or submit in the next block) to call disputeTree again, immediately re-locking the contract.

distinct_impacts.description: setDisputeAmount reverts while disputer != address(0), so Governor calls consistently revert.
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: The function setDisputeAmount reverts if disputer != address(0).

distinct_impacts.description: Attacker can sustain the lock at linear cost (e.g., current disputeAmount per cycle).
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: the attacker can block parameter updates indefinitely at a linear cost (e.g., current disputeAmount per cycle).
